newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian interim PM to visit Skopje on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian interim PM to visit Skopje on Thursday.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski will pay a two-day visit to the neighbouring former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia, the government said in a statement on Wednesday.
Sofianski is expected to meet his Macedonian counterpart Branko Crvenkovski on Thursday to discuss ways to increase economic ties.
The two Balkan countries, struggling with the transition to a market economy, both seek investors to complete regional infrastructure projects.

A railway link between Sofia and Skopje has yet to be completed. It is part of a route from Turkey to the Bulgarian Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas via Bulgaria and Macedonia to Durres in Albania.
A million-dollar East-West highway is planned to link southern Italian ports by road and rail via Albania and Macedonia with Turkey and via Bulgarian Black Sea ports with former Soviet republics.
Bulgaria and Macedonia have not signed intergovernmental agreements in recent years because Skopje insists on signing the documents in Bulgarian and Macedonian.
Bulgaria, which has complex historical relations with the former Yugoslav republic, refuses to recognise the Macedonian language, which it considers a dialect of Bulgarian.
It does however recognise Macedonia as an independent state.
Sofianski's visit will be the first by a head of government since mid-1993, when Lyuben Berov visited Skopje.
